mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the previous month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the previous month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals severe labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is above 3%, it signals stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and CPIAUCSL > 3%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 is negative for 2 quarters and CPIAUCSL is above 3%.
